name: Amsterdam
industries: Banking, travel and payments technology, and the Schiphol logistics complex drive one of Europe's most agile-mature markets.
intro:
Amsterdam's claim on agile history is direct — ING's enterprise-wide agile reorganisation here became the model banks worldwide copied — and the city's delivery market still runs ahead of the continent. Tech firms along the Zuidas and in the harbour district, the payments and travel giants born here, and the airport-logistics complex at Schiphol all hire Scrum-credentialed professionals as standard; programme managers with PMP anchor the infrastructure and energy-transition portfolios. Dutch directness extends to hiring: the certificate is checked first. We run live online cohorts throughout the year on Amsterdam-friendly hours — weekend Saturday–Sunday batches and midweek Wednesday–Thursday batches both — meaning learners in Amsterdam attend at ordinary local times, never overnight; the table below shows each upcoming date converted for Amsterdam. Afterwards we support the exam application, drill full-length mocks, and keep the trainer on call for doubts until you pass.

Amsterdam's project demand rides on three rails: the tech companies that made the city their European base, the banks and payment firms native to it, and the logistics complex stretching from Schiphol to the port corridor. All three run internationally staffed programs in English, where recognized certification travels across borders better than local references do. The course is live online across two consecutive days in central European hours. Dutch salaries for certified project professionals are strong and transparent; the sourced Amsterdam entries below give you dated, named figures for negotiation. The employer list shows the tech-finance-logistics spread hiring certified talent here, and internationally distributed teams headquartered in Amsterdam can run private cohorts across their offices.
